teacherNotes.title: Core Words
teacherNotes.content: wake up, get up, shower, dress, breakfast, lunch, dinner, work, study, return, sleep

elements.content: Core Active Vocabulary (10-20 items):
wake up, get up, shower, dress, breakfast, lunch, dinner, work, study, return, sleep
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• I wake up at seven o'clock (stating wake-up time)
• I have breakfast in the kitchen (stating morning routine)
• I leave home at eight thirty (stating departure)
• I go to bed at eleven PM (stating sleep time)

teacherNotes.title: Phonetic Focus
teacherNotes.content: Pronunciation of 'breakfast' /ˈbrek.fəst/ and verb endings (-s in 3rd person).

teacherNotes.title: Grammar Function
teacherNotes.content: Present Simple for Habits & Daily Actions ('I wake up at 7:00', 'She has breakfast')

elements.content: Grammar System & Functional Framing:
Present Simple for Habits & Daily Actions ('I wake up at 7:00', 'She has breakfast')
Controlled Practice:
First you open your eyes in bed in the morning. What do you do?
Reading Script & Dialogue:

A: What time do you usually wake up?
B: I wake up at seven o'clock, take a shower, and have breakfast.
A: When do you start work?
B: I start work at nine and finish at five in the evening.
Listening Comprehension:
Listen to a vlogger describing their daily routine and order the sequence of activities.

elements.content: Timestamped Multi-Duration Flows:

• 60m Flow (Essential): 0-10m Warm-up & Goal; 10-25m Vocab & Chunks; 25-40m Grammar Practice; 40-55m Speaking Pair Task; 55-60m Cool-down.
• 90m Flow (Expanded): 0-10m Warm-up; 10-30m 5-step Vocab Drills; 30-50m Grammar Workshop; 50-70m Roleplay; 70-85m Writing; 85-90m Wrap-up.
• 120m Flow (Full Workshop): 0-15m Icebreaker; 15-40m Vocab Lab; 40-70m Grammar Simulation; 70-100m Group Activity; 100-115m Writing Portfolio; 115-120m Reflection.
